title: Integrated AlphaHoldem Seed2 one-million-hand replication
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: An untouched second lineage continued from 263,905 to at least 1,048,576 actual environment hands with the identical integrated AlphaHoldem recipe will reproduce the positive broad late-stage slope seen in Seed1, with a positive pooled 263k-to-1M matched slope, at least three of four nonnegative anchor slopes, both seats nonnegative, and preserved Standard10 capability.

result.summary: Seed2 exact-state continuation completed uninterrupted at1,048,795 actual environment hands. All22 training-integrity gates and Standard10 preservation passed. The fresh65,536-hand matched panel had pooled slope+2.2529 bb/100 but only2/4 nonnegative anchors and negative seat1, so the preregistered replication gate failed. Across Seed1 and Seed2 both pooled slopes were positive with mean+2.4887, but the two-seed t95 interval[-0.5077,+5.4852], Standard10 mean-2.8473, and seat1 mean-0.3121 do not support unchanged scaling.
result.conclusion: One-million-hand training is not a mechanistic failure: both independent lineages improved their pooled four-anchor result and preserved Standard10 logits closely. However breadth did not reproduce, and both lineages degraded relative performance against the strongest Standard10 anchor while Seed2 also regressed in seat1. The evidence supports continuing the long-horizon learned-policy family, but not simply allocating more hands to the unchanged objective.
result.next_step: Use frozen assignments, metrics, archives, and raw matched rows to localize Standard10 exposure and seat-specific objective conflict; then preregister the smallest Standard10/seat-balance intervention with geometric multi-seed gates before any larger scale or Slumbot spend.
